stories.title: Google’s Atlas of the human genome could pave the way for new treatments
stories.simple_summary: Google created an AI tool that maps human DNA to help scientists understand diseases better and develop new treatments.
stories.why_it_matters: This is very early-stage research; it won't affect you immediately, but it could lead to better medicines and treatments for diseases in the future.

stories.title: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
stories.simple_summary: Adobe made it easier to use AI in their Premiere video editing software so video editors can generate videos, sound effects, and music without having to switch between tools.
stories.why_it_matters: If you edit videos professionally or run a video business, this could save you time — but it's only useful if you already use Adobe Premiere.

stories.title: China’s top court sets out new AI red lines with rules on deepfakes and privacy
stories.simple_summary: China's top court created new rules about AI that limit deepfakes (fake videos of people) and protect people's privacy.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you do business in China, this is mostly relevant to government and large tech companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Opinion | Nowhere to hide: AI blurs the rules of anonymity
stories.simple_summary: An opinion piece warns that AI is making it harder for people to stay anonymous online because AI can identify who you are from small clues.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters if you care about privacy online — it's a reminder that AI can recognize people even when you try to hide your identity.

stories.title: The Pentagon Asked OpenAI for Artificial Intelligence Designed to Rarely Say No
stories.simple_summary: The Pentagon (U.S. military) asked OpenAI to create AI that would agree with requests instead of refusing them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to government policy discussions — nothing that affects your daily life or business.

stories.title: AI will cure cancer in our lifetime, claims boss of UK chip giant
stories.simple_summary: The boss of a British chip company claimed that AI will cure cancer in our lifetimes.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an optimistic prediction from someone trying to promote his company — take it with a grain of salt, and don't count on it happening soon.

stories.title: The House Democrat who's making AI regulation her No. 1 priority
stories.simple_summary: A U.S. House Democrat is making AI rules and regulation her top priority in government.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters if you care about how AI gets regulated in the U.S., but it's mostly about politics right now — no immediate changes for your business.

stories.title: French AI company Mistral hits $24 billion valuation in funding round
stories.simple_summary: A French AI company called Mistral raised money and is now valued at $24 billion (this is an investor valuation, not money they actually have).
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
stories.simple_summary: A tech news site is explaining AI jargon and terms people should know.
stories.why_it_matters: If you want to understand AI terms better, this could be a helpful reference article.

stories.title: Nvidia CEO Says GPT-6 Astra Brings AGI Closer
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia's CEO said that a new AI model called GPT-6 Astra is bringing us closer to AGI (Artificial General Intelligence — AI that can do almost anything humans can do).
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly hype and relevant to tech investors — not something that affects your life today.

stories.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
stories.simple_summary: Early tests show that a drug created by AI might slow down aging in people.
stories.why_it_matters: This is very early research and not proven yet — but it's promising and could lead to new anti-aging treatments down the road.

stories.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement
stories.simple_summary: Two newspapers (Seattle Times and Newsday) are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using their news articles to train AI without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a journalist or media company, this matters because it could affect whether AI companies can use your work — for others, it's a legal case between big companies.
